articles.title: Why US soldiers keep killing women in Okinawa — and why they go unpunished
articles.author: Amanda Yee
articles.content_excerpt: In October, 39-year-old Ann Yagi was found dead in a Naha hotel. Shortly after, US marine Devin Jacob Ballard was arrested on charges of murder-robbery. But the Yagi’s killing reignited a decades-old question Okinawa can’t escape: Who pays the price for Washington’s military bases? Okinawan scholar and peace activist Keiko Yonaha joins Amanda Yee to lay out what the headlines leave out — countless sexual assaults by US soldiers and near-total impunity, a Japanese government that covers up case after case, and what Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi’s rapid militarization means for an island already marked as a potential battlefield. articles.title: Algeria sends troops to Niger as security ties deepen
articles.author: Pavan Kulkarni
articles.content_excerpt: On October 30, the first convoy of Algerian troops arrived in its southern neighbor Niger as security ties continue to deepen between the two countries. It is Algeria’s first foreign deployment since it sent troops to Egypt during the 1973 Arab-Israeli war. The deployment was approved by both houses of the parliament on October 25. “Niger’s security is part of Algeria’s security,” said Foreign Minister Ahmed Attaf, who tabled the proposal before legislators. Algeria shares a 951 km-long border with Niger in the Sahara Desert, which became a hotbed for terror groups after the destruction of Libya by NATO powers in 2011. articles.title: Over 4,000 arrested under Palestine Action ban
articles.author: Ana Vračar
articles.content_excerpt: New arrests of Palestine solidarity activists on October 31 brought the total number of arrests related to the Palestine Action ban in Britain to over 4,000, advocacy groups warned on Saturday. The arrests were made during an action in front of the US embassy in London, as law enforcement agencies once again decided to charge protesters holding signs expressing their opposition to the genocide in Gaza. The action was mirrored in the proximity of the US consulate in Edinburgh, where no arrests were made on the day. Since July 2025 – when Keir Starmer’s government proscribed direct action group Palestine Action – police forces around the country have disrupted peaceful protests against the ban. articles.title: The Cultural Apparatus, Materialist Aesthetics, and the Critique of Eurocentrism
articles.author: Jamil Jonna
articles.content_excerpt: John Bellamy Foster discusses the tradition of cultural analysis in Monthly Review with Jennifer Ponce de León and Gabriel Rockhill. “ MR ‘s approach…over its long history,” Foster explains, “has been a product of its deep commitment to historical materialism.” Drawing parallels between Bertolt Brecht’s observations during Hitler’s rise in Germany and an analysis of MAGA-style fascism under Trump today, it becomes clear that “control of the intellectual and cultural life of the nation is integral to the neofascist project.” However, there is also hope, as culture “constantly emerges from below in revolutionary new forms, which cannot be entirely repressed.” The post The Cultural Apparatus, Materialist Aesthetics, and the Critique of Eurocentrism appeared first on Monthly Review .

articles.title: Nietzsche’s French Legacy: Fascism and the Compatible Left
articles.author: Jamil Jonna
articles.content_excerpt: MR is pleased to be able to share with readers Gabriel Rockhill’s Introduction to The Poverty of Left Nietzscheanism by Aymeric Monville (Iskra Books, 2026). Rockhill provides readers with a thorough account of the rehabilitation of Nietzsche within French Theory and its consequences within the non-communist left. Fascism, Rockhill argues, “can only be understood and contested through materialist analysis and anticapitalist praxis”—a fitting preamble to a book that acts as “an insightful indictment of the dominant capitalist ideologies while clearly articulating the political path forward.” The post Nietzsche’s French Legacy: Fascism and the Compatible Left appeared first on Monthly Review .

articles.title: Foreword to ‘The Exterminating Empire’
articles.author: Jamil Jonna
articles.content_excerpt: In this stirring foreword to Chris Kaspar de Ploeg’s The Exterminating Empire (Monthly Review Press, 2026), Jason Hickel decries a world in which cruelty, genocide, and rapacious capitalism have become de rigueur, seemingly with no consequences for the Western elites perpetuating these atrocities in the Global South. “The narrative of ‘double standards,'” Hickel writes, “presupposes that they have at least some shred of morality. But they do not. For them there is but one standard: the law of capital.” The post Foreword to ‘The Exterminating Empire’ appeared first on Monthly Review .
